# LeakSanitizer suppressions. Every entry needs a named allocation stack and
# a written rationale; anything not listed here is a failure.
#
# Rationale: the C-ABI panic containment seam deliberately `mem::forget`s the
# panic payload after catching it (see src/entrypoint.rs and
# src/module_data.rs). A payload's destructor can itself panic and unwind
# across the pam_sm_* C boundary, so the small payload allocation (a boxed
# static string, 16 bytes per contained panic) is intentionally leaked
# instead of dropped. The panic-containment tests trigger this path on
# purpose, so LSan sees the allocation with no free. Product code never
# leaks; only the test-driven containment path does, bounded by the number
# of deliberately injected panics.
leak:*StaticStrPayload*
